subject: history
topicName: Women and the Family in Nazi Germany

questions.question: Explain two ways the Nazis encouraged women to have more children. (4 marks)

points.text: Marriage loans (June 1933): offered 1,000 marks to couples if the wife gave up work; 25% of the loan was cancelled for each child born, so four children meant the entire loan was wiped out. The Mother's Cross (August 1938): awarded to mothers who had many children - bronze for 4+, silver for 6+, gold for 8+ children - giving social status and privileges to mothers.

questions.question: How far did Nazi policies improve the lives of German women? (8 marks)

points.text: Nazi policies improved life for some women: marriage loans provided financial help, the Mother's Cross gave recognition to mothers, and family allowances supported larger families. questions.question: "The Nazis failed to control women's employment." How far do you agree? (12 marks)

points.text: The Nazis did fail to control women's employment in practice. Despite policies to remove women from work (dismissal from civil service, marriage loans requiring women to leave jobs), the number of women in employment actually increased from 11.5 million (1933) to 12.7 million (1939). questions.question: Explain how the war changed women's roles in Nazi Germany. (8 marks)

points.text: The war dramatically changed women's roles. With millions of men conscripted, women were needed in factories, farms, and offices. By 1943, 52% of the workforce was female. From 1943, women were conscripted for war work. The Nazis had to abandon their ideology that women belonged in the home. questions.question: "Nazi policies towards women were contradictory." How far do you agree? (16 marks)

points.text: Nazi policies were deeply contradictory. The Nazis preached that women should stay at home (the Three Ks), yet the economy needed women to work. They dismissed women from professions, yet by 1939 more women were employed than in 1933. They promoted motherhood, yet the birth rate never returned to Weimar levels and was declining by 1939.
